title: Claims Training Notes: How Rideshare Days Count toward a Cardinal Rental Reimbursement Day Room
content:
Rideshare days are weighted by what they cost when they are counted against the day room of a loss under Cardinal Rental Reimbursement. The figures come from the rideshare, taxi and transit reimbursements on the claim's rental ledger: the days billed on them and the amounts reimbursed.

**Rule.** The weighting depends on the average reimbursed per rideshare day billed:
- rideshare reimbursements on the claim average no more than 0.5 of the option's daily limit per day billed: each rideshare day billed counts as 0.5 of a day;
- they average more than 0.5 of the daily limit but no more than the daily limit: each counts as 0.75 of a day;
- otherwise: each counts as a full day.

The weighted rideshare days are rounded up to a whole day.

## Questions answered

**How is the average found?**
The total reimbursed for rideshare, taxi and transit on the claim, divided by the rideshare days billed on the claim.

**What about an average exactly at a boundary?**
Each boundary includes its own figure. An average exactly at half the daily limit takes 0.5. An average exactly at the daily limit takes 0.75.

**What happens to a fraction of a day?**
It is rounded up. For example, 3.75 weighted days count as 4.

## Worked figures (hypothetical, Cardinal Rental Reimbursement 40/1200, $40.00 daily limit)

| Rideshare days billed | Reimbursed | Average per day | Weight | Weighted days counted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | $70.00 | $17.50 | 0.5 | 2 |
| 4 | $80.00 | $20.00 | 0.5 | 2 |
| 5 | $150.00 | $30.00 | 0.75 | 4 (3.75 rounded up) |
| 3 | $126.00 | $42.00 | 1 | 3 |
